newsitem.title: MEXICO: Eight rural Mexicans massacred in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Eight rural Mexicans massacred in ambush.

text.p: Eight Mexicans were gunned down in an ambush in the mountains of the volatile southwestern state of Guerrero, authorities said on Sunday.
The attack occurred on Saturday in the remote town of San Bartolo in the municipality of San Miguel Totolapan, an area of heavily armed guerrillas and drug traffickers.
San Miguel Totolapan Mayor Egdy Julian Gomez said troops were in the town and investigators on their way to examine the bodies.

Gomez said the sheriff of a neighbouring town heard his brother had been killed in San Miguel Totolapan and went to investigate with six other men. When they found the dead brother, the sheriff and his party were ambushed and killed, he said.
The rural area in the mountains north of the world famous Pacific Coast resort of Acapulco is known for the cultivation of marijuana and poppy flowers, the raw material for heroin.
The South Sierra Madre mountains are also the home of a leftist guerrilla group called the Popular Revolutionary Army.
